xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5111: Push notifications: keep a sent-push history, mark withdrawn questions, and show unreachable linked machines in Needs you

plan.title: Push notifications: keep a sent-push history, mark withdrawn questions, and show unreachable linked machines in Needs you
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The operator filed one incident fix (PAN-5111) with one acceptance list covering push history, withdrawn questions and unreachable machines. The plan splits it into two vertical slices (A: push history, items 1-7; B: unreachable machines, items 8-11) that share no source files and no edges, so the work agent can run them in parallel. About 42 files: most are the test file each item carries, and the subsystem count is inflated because every top-level doc page (configuration/*.mdx, changelog.mdx, docs/*.md) counts as its own subsystem.

narratives.Problem: On 2026-11-10 the operator got two needs-you pushes while Needs you was empty. Overdeck keeps sent pushes only in memory, records nothing when a pushed question leaves without an answer, and shows no sign when it cannot fetch a linked machine's Needs-You (only dashboard.log has it). The phone cannot read fleet Needs-You at all (403 through the channel).
narratives.Proposal: Slice A: a push history module appends sent and resolved lines to ~/.overdeck/logs/push-sent.jsonl (5 MiB rotation); the dispatcher records every delivered push with per-provider outcomes and, 10 s after a pushed auq:/plan:/perm: key leaves its last owner, records answered (an Overdeck answer door noted it) or resolved-without-answer; GET /api/push/history (read:conversations) serves the last 50 with a derived state; Settings -> Anywhere -> Phone notifications shows Recent notifications with Waiting / Answered / Answered or withdrawn and Open links. Slice B: the linked Needs-You sync remembers fetch failures; GET /api/fleet/needs-you adds unreachable[] for non-offline links with a failure and serves a paired phone that list only; desktop and phone Needs you show "Can't reach <machine>; it may have items waiting." Docs cover both. See .pan/drafts/pan-5111.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to which pushes are sent, their wording, dedup or rate limit.
- No resolution tracking across a dashboard restart beyond the derived state (D-8).
- No answer notes for plan approvals, permission prompts or the pi ask modal; no edits to src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts.
- No change to refuseFleetRequest; linked machines and connectors still cannot read fleet Needs-You.
- The phone does not receive other machines' Needs-you rows.
- No Can't reach signal in MCP tools, the CLI or the phone Live Activity count.
- No retry or polling added to the linked Needs-You sync.
- No history export, search, delete or retention setting.
- No question text (notification body or preview) is ever written to the history file.

autoDecisions.summary: 'Settings -> Notifications' maps to Settings -> Anywhere -> Phone notifications (PushPanel); the list is a new RecentNotifications component at its bottom.
autoDecisions.rationale: PushPanel is the only push settings surface; the desktop Notifications block is browser event toggles.

autoDecisions.summary: History is append-only JSONL with 'sent' and 'resolved' lines joined by a per-entry UUID, folded at read time; rotation renames to push-sent.jsonl.1 at 5 MiB and loads read .1 then the current file.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keys repeat (perm:pending per subject, re-pushes), so only an id joins reliably; reading both files keeps 'last 50' across a rotation.

autoDecisions.summary: Every delivered push is recorded (questions, approvals, edges, summaries, Send test); primed, filtered, rate-limited and active-elsewhere items are not.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for every push sent; undelivered items were never sent.

autoDecisions.summary: History stores title, never body or publicTitle; deliveries keep provider, target, ok, reason and status only (no provider detail or rejection message); a push that reached no target is not recorded.
autoDecisions.rationale: D-8 of PAN-2354 keeps question text off disk; provider detail can carry raw request errors, URLs or tokens (plan critique round 1).

autoDecisions.summary: 'answered' only when an Overdeck answer door (agent answer-question after a successful delivery, conversation message whose answersToolUseId is verified pending, Codex app-server approval after its id check) noted the verified auq: key inside the push's answer window; every other departure, including all plan: and perm: keys, is 'resolved-without-answer' shown as 'Answered or withdrawn'. pi ask is skipped.
autoDecisions.rationale: A terminal answer and a withdrawn question look identical to the dashboard; the issue's own label covers both. Plan-action routes carry no toolUseId; ohmypi support is being removed.

autoDecisions.summary: Answer notes are non-consuming timestamps matched against an answer window (delivery to departure + 10 s, closed early by a re-push); resolutions wait 10 s and dispose() records them at once.
autoDecisions.rationale: Removes the transcript/answer race and stops a re-pushed key from crediting the wrong push (plan critique round 1).

autoDecisions.summary: Entry state is derived at read time: resolved line; else tracked or pending now => open; else resolved-without-answer once the service is warm (60 s and one conversation scan); else null. The dispatcher re-adopts open entries for primed keys after a restart. The conversation scan keeps running without targets while it tracks conversation entries (notify: false).
autoDecisions.rationale: Overdeck stores no status it can derive; a restart must not label a still-pending question withdrawn, and losing all targets must not freeze an entry at Waiting (plan critique round 1).

autoDecisions.summary: GET /api/push/history is scoped read:conversations and mirrors PAN-5093's route coupling (ROUTE_SCOPES, no-loss matrix, TELEMETRY_CLIENT_ROUTES, docs/TELEMETRY.md).
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names the scope and the no-loss row; telemetry.ts says its list holds every ROUTE_SCOPES path.

autoDecisions.summary: A Can't reach row needs a recorded Needs-You fetch failure whose last attempt is at most 60 minutes old, on a link that is not revoked or hidden; no offline filter; 404 and success clear it; prune drops it.
autoDecisions.rationale: The logged incident is a flapping link (online/connecting/offline per link-supervisor.ts), so an offline filter would make the row blink; fetches repeat on every connect and heartbeat, keeping a live failure fresh, while a switched-off machine stops producing attempts and expires within an hour. A machine that goes offline without a failed fetch still adds nothing (PAN-4651 NFR-2).

autoDecisions.summary: The row is non-blocking, joins the desktop System group, and counts in the Needs-you count.
autoDecisions.rationale: It is not an agent waiting on an answer, like the disk alert it sits beside.

autoDecisions.summary: A paired phone channel caller may read GET /api/fleet/needs-you but gets only { machines: [], unreachable }; all other channel callers are still refused; refuseFleetRequest is unchanged.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires the row on the phone, which today gets 403; the phone cannot open other machines' rows anyway. Same pattern as fleetSpawnGate's connector exception (PAN-4950 D-5).

autoDecisions.summary: Keep both slices in one issue with plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of filing a sibling issue.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator filed one incident fix with one acceptance list; the slices share no files or edges so they run in parallel.

items.title: Add the push history module that appends and folds push-sent.jsonl

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. Add PushDelivery (provider, target, ok, reason?, status?; no detail), PushSentRecord, PushResolutionOutcome, PushResolutionRecord and PushHistorySink (recordSent, recordResolution, openEntryIdFor) to src/lib/push/types.ts. Create src/lib/push/push-history.ts exporting PUSH_HISTORY_FILE, PUSH_HISTORY_MAX_BYTES (5 MiB), PUSH_HISTORY_RECENT_LIMIT (50), PushEntryState, PushHistoryEntry, PushHistory (adds recent, ready, flush), createPushHistory({ dir?, maxBytes? }), getPushHistory() (singleton under join(getOverdeckHome(),'logs')), PushStateContext and pushEntryState(entry, ctx). JSONL lines carry v:1 and type 'sent'|'resolved' joined by id (D-2). Memory updates synchronously; writes go through one promise chain (lazy load of .1 then current file; newest 200 sent kept; rotate by rename past maxBytes (D-5); appendFile 0o600 after mkdir 0o700). recordSent writes only the listed fields and drops any extra property such as detail (D-4). openEntryIdFor returns the newest unresolved entry for the key (and subject for perm: keys). pushEntryState follows D-8 (resolution; tracked or pending => open; warm => resolved-without-answer; else null). No *Sync calls; errors logged, never thrown.

items.title: Given a recordSent call, when the queue flushes, then push-sent.jsonl contains one line with id, ts, kind, category, key, subject, title, issueId, url and deliveries and no body field
Given a delivery passed with detail 'token=SENTINEL-SECRET', when the queue flushes, then the file does not contain SENTINEL-SECRET
Given a small maxBytes, when an append would cross it, then the file is renamed to push-sent.jsonl.1 and recent() on a fresh instance returns entries from both files newest first
Given an unresolved entry for key auq:t1, then openEntryIdFor returns its id, and after a resolved line for it, openEntryIdFor returns null

pushEntryState returns null for a journal: key and for an untracked, not pending, not warm entry, 'open' when tracked or pending, the stored outcome when resolved, and 'resolved-without-answer' when warm
Add the in-memory operator answer note registry with time windows

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2, D-7. Create src/lib/push/operator-answers.ts exporting noteOperatorAnswer(key, now?), operatorAnsweredBetween(key, fromMs, toMs, now?) (non-consuming) and resetOperatorAnswers() for tests. Map<key, number[]> of note times; at most 10 times per key; drop times older than 24 h on every call; at most 500 keys (evict the oldest-inserted key); ignore an empty key.

items.title: Given a note at t=1000, when operatorAnsweredBetween is called with [500, 1500], then it returns true, and with [1001, 2000] it returns false
Given the same window queried twice, then both calls return true (notes are never consumed)
Given a note older than 24 h, then operatorAnsweredBetween returns false; given 501 keys, then the oldest key returns false
Record verified operator answer notes at the agent answer, conversation message and Codex approval doors

expected_outputs: the three server test files pass

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3, D-6. Notes name only the question a door verified and delivered to, after delivery succeeded. (1) permissions.ts handlePostAgentAnswerQuestion: plain branch keeps deliverAgentMessage's result and notes `auq:${questionSet.toolId}` only when delivery.ok; operator-decision branch notes after its !result.ok refusal; HTTP responses unchanged; Deft branches no note. (2) conversation-message.ts: rename the body to non-exported deliverConversationMessage; the exported handleConversationMessage checks before delivery that body.answersToolUseId is in getPendingQuestions(sessionFile) (resolveSessionFile from deps; false on any error) and notes it only when verified and response.status < 300. (3) conversation-delivery.ts handleConversationCodexApproval: app-server branch only, after postCodexAppServerOp and the id check, note `auq:${expectedToolUseId}`. (4) frontend pendingInputAnswer.ts sends answersToolUseId with the /message body when toolUseId is set. Update the exact-body assertion in MobileNeedsYou.test.tsx (about line 258) and any other test pinning 'Operator answered the pending question'. Do NOT edit src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts.

items.title: Given an agent answer whose delivery returns ok, then a note exists for auq:<matched toolId>; given deliverAgentMessage returning { ok: false }, then no note exists
Given a plain agent question answered with a stale toolUseId, then the note names the question actually answered and no note exists for the stale id
Given a conversation message whose answersToolUseId is pending and delivery succeeds, then a note exists; given a stale answersToolUseId, then no note exists
Given a Codex app-server approval with the matching id, then a note exists for auq:<expectedToolUseId>; given a mismatched id, then the handler returns 409 and no note exists
buildPendingAnswerRequest for a claude-code conversation with toolUseId returns a body containing answersToolUseId, and without toolUseId a body without it
Make the dispatcher record delivered pushes and resolve departed keys inside answer windows

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4, D-3, D-4, D-7, D-8, D-8a. Optional deps history?: PushHistorySink, wasAnswered?: (key, fromMs, toMs) => boolean, newId?. Export RESOLVE_GRACE_MS = 10_000; add trackedIds(), isPending(subject, key), tracksConversations() and observeSubject(subject, items, { notify? }). fanOut builds deliveries with provider, target, ok, reason, status only (rejected provider => ok:false reason 'error'; never detail or message). deliver records a sent record only when deliveries.length > 0, else drops the tracked id. Track delivered keys with deliveredAt; a re-push closes earlier scheduled windows (windowEnd = now). Primed items adopt history.openEntryIdFor(subject, key). notify:false processes departures only. Departure (unique key: last owner gone; else per subject) schedules resolveNow after RESOLVE_GRACE_MS with windowEnd = departure + grace; resolveNow uses wasAnswered(key, deliveredAt, windowEnd). dispose() runs scheduled resolutions at once. Edges/summary/sendNow record subject null and never resolve. Fake timers in tests.

items.title: Given a delivered question and a rejected provider whose error contains SENTINEL-SECRET, then one sent record is recorded with ok:false reason 'error' for that provider and no stored field contains SENTINEL-SECRET
Given a primed item, a filtered kind, a rate-limited item, and a push whose providers return no outcomes, then no sent record is recorded
Given an auq: key owned by two subjects, when both drop it and 10 s pass, then exactly one resolution is recorded, and none before the second owner drops it
Given leave, re-push and an answer note before the first timer fires, then the first entry resolves 'resolved-without-answer' and the second resolves 'answered' after it leaves

Given a primed key with an open history entry, when it departs, then a resolution is recorded for that entry's id; given observeSubject with notify false, then a new key is not pushed and a tracked departure still resolves; given dispose() during the grace, then the resolution is recorded at once
Wire history, answer windows and the no-target departure scan into the push service

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5, D-8, D-8a. startNeedsYouPushService deps gain history?: PushHistory (default getPushHistory()) and now?; call void history.ready(); pass history and wasAnswered: operatorAnsweredBetween to the dispatcher; ServiceState keeps history, startedAt, scanCompleted. scanConversations runs when hasTargets() or dispatcher.tracksConversations(), passes { notify } (notify = hasTargets) to both observeSubject calls, and sets scanCompleted after a pass. The sendTestPush fallback gets history. Export WARM_AFTER_MS = 60_000, PushHistoryView and getPushHistoryView(limit = 50) building PushStateContext (trackedIds, isPending, warm = scanCompleted && now - startedAt >= WARM_AFTER_MS).

items.title: Given a conversation question delivered through the service, when getPushHistoryView() runs, then the entry has state 'open', and after the feed drops it, 10 s pass and the service is warm, then state 'resolved-without-answer'
Given noteOperatorAnswer('auq:<id>') before the departure, then getPushHistoryView() returns state 'answered'
Given the providers report no targets after a push, when the tracked question leaves the feed, then a resolution is recorded and a new question in the feed records no sent line

Given a restart while the question is still pending (primed), then getPushHistoryView() returns state 'open' for the old entry and its later departure records a resolution for that id; an untracked, not-pending entry before warm returns state null
Serve the last 50 pushes at GET /api/push/history

Add pushHistoryRoute (GET /api/push/history, rejectUnauthorizedDashboardRequest, no-store, body { entries: await getPushHistoryView() }) to pushRouteLayer and fix the push.ts header (only this route is in ROUTE_SCOPES). items.title: Given an authorized request, when GET /api/push/history runs, then it returns 200 with an entries array and Cache-Control no-store
requiredScopeFor('GET', '/api/push/history') returns 'read:conversations'
NO_LOSS_MATRIX contains a 'GET /api/push/history' http row, and TELEMETRY_CLIENT_ROUTES and docs/TELEMETRY.md both list /api/push/history
Show Recent notifications in Settings -> Anywhere -> Phone notifications

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7, D-1. pushApi.ts: PushHistoryEntry type mirroring PushHistoryView, PUSH_HISTORY_QUERY_KEY, loadPushHistory(). New RecentNotifications.tsx (10 s refetch): section data-component='recent-notifications', h4 'Recent notifications', empty text 'No notifications sent yet.', each li data-push-id with title, relative time, delivery text ('Delivered to N' | 'Not delivered', plus ', N failed (reason status)') and state text (none for null; open 'Waiting', answered 'Answered', resolved-without-answer 'Answered or withdrawn' with the PRD tooltip), and an Open link built with decisionSubjectPath/navigateToDecisionSubject (conv:<name> => conversation; agent subject or null with issueId => issue). items.title: Given history entries with each state, when RecentNotifications renders, then the texts 'Waiting', 'Answered' and 'Answered or withdrawn' appear on their rows
Given an entry with two ok deliveries, then its row shows 'Delivered to 2'; given one failed delivery with reason gone and status 410, then it shows 'Not delivered, 1 failed (gone 410)'
Given an entry with subject 'conv:my-conv', then its row has an Open link with href '/conv/my-conv'

scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt contains src/components/Settings/anywhere/__tests__/RecentNotifications.test.tsx
Remember each linked machine's Needs-You fetch failure until a success, 404 or prune

narrative.Action: PRD WI-8, D-10. Export LinkedNeedsYouFailure { since, lastAttemptAt, reason } (ISO strings); add deps.now (default Date.now) and failureFor(environmentId) to LinkedNeedsYouSync. fetchOnce: thrown fetch records the error message; 404 clears; other non-200 records `answered <status>`; malformed body records 'sent a malformed Needs-You feed'; a stored feed clears. A repeated failure keeps the first since and moves lastAttemptAt. prune also clears failures. Keep every existing deps.log call; update the header.

items.title: Given a fetch that throws 'Secure channel did not open', when onConnect runs, then failureFor returns that reason with ISO since and lastAttemptAt
Given a second failure, then since keeps the first failure's time and lastAttemptAt moves; given a later 200 feed, then failureFor returns null
Given a 404 answer, then failureFor returns null; given a 500 answer, then the reason is 'answered 500'
Given prune([]), then failureFor returns null for the pruned link
Return unreachable links from fleet Needs-You and let a paired phone read that list

narrative.Action: PRD WI-9, D-10, D-12 (auth surface). FleetAwarenessDeps gains optional needsYouFailure (default currentLinkedNeedsYou()?.failureFor(env) ?? null) and optional now (default Date.now). Export UNREACHABLE_FRESH_MS = 3_600_000 and UnreachableMachine. buildFleetNeedsYou returns { machines, unreachable }: machines unchanged; unreachable lists links that are not revoked (record or status state), not hidden, and have a failure whose lastAttemptAt is at most UNREACHABLE_FRESH_MS old, in store order. Do NOT filter on 'offline': a flapping link moves online/connecting/offline and the row must not blink (D-10). The route body: if channelOfRequest(request) !== null and resolveRequestCredential(request)?.kind === 'phone', run rejectUnauthorizedDashboardRequest and answer { machines: [], unreachable }; otherwise refuseFleetRequest as today. refuseFleetRequest itself is unchanged. Update the header (NFR-2 amended). Update the existing 'offline link contributes no rows' expectation to include unreachable: []. New route test follows fleet-connector.test.ts (mocked channelOfRequest, createAccessToken).

items.title: Given an online link and an offline link, each with a failure 5 minutes old, when buildFleetNeedsYou runs, then unreachable contains both with environmentId, label, since and reason
Given a failure whose lastAttemptAt is 61 minutes old, a revoked link and a hidden link, then none appears in unreachable
Given a phone token through a mocked channel, when GET /api/fleet/needs-you runs, then it returns 200 with machines [] and the unreachable list
Given a machine token through a mocked channel, when GET /api/fleet/needs-you runs, then it returns 403 'a linked machine cannot use the fleet routes here'
Show a Can't reach card in the desktop Needs you System group
